usual_baseline: About half operated within 36 hours (41% [1132], 54% [1595]); mean time to theatre 43–53 hours, up to 80 hours in a major trauma centre [1184]. Commonest causes: no theatre space (28–51% of delays [1130][1481]) and anticoagulation. DOAC patients waited a median 39 h vs 25 h [1697].
fix_that_works: Structural change. Two extra morning trauma lists: 41% to 78% within 36 h, mean 49 to 27 h [1132][1499]. Anaesthetic 'hot week': 54% to 87.5% within 36 h [1595]. Daytime emergency theatre: delays 49% to 26% [1130][1532]. Nurse-led IV vitamin K in ED: mean 53.71 to 37.61 h [1506].
fix_that_fails: Multicomponent bundle cut mean time from 80 to 55 h, but delays rose from 57.4% to 63.9% [1184]. Anaesthesia outreach sped consults but not surgery (within 48 h 38% to 51.6%, p=0.904) [1618]. INR sample education: rejection 16.5% to 11.1%, not significant [1718].
consultant_advice: Heavily overdone, and the answer is always theatre capacity. Don't audit the overall time again. Audit a single cause instead: DOAC and warfarin pathways, rejected INR samples, or whether pre-op echo requests are appropriate [1731].
